FAQ

Frequently asked questions

The questions we actually get — answered honestly.
Starting point

South Africa

Next chapter

Russia

How long does the application process take?

Typically 3–6 months from initial consultation to admission letter. Scholarship (Quota) applications have specific deadlines set by the Russian Government, usually closing in January for September intake. We keep you on track so nothing slips through the cracks.

Is my degree recognised in South Africa?

Yes — with proper planning. Medical graduates need HPCSA registration. Engineering graduates need ECSA evaluation. We guide you through this process from day one, not as an afterthought. Recognition is a strategy, not a surprise.

Do I need to speak Russian before I go?

Not necessarily. Many programs offer preparatory Russian language courses. We provide pre-departure language support and connect you with resources to hit the ground running. Survival Russian is enough to start; academic Russian comes with time.

What if I struggle academically or personally?

Our student support team can help with wellness and in-country logistics. We check in regularly, provide support, and help address challenges before small issues become big problems. We're not ghosting you after arrival.

Are there really no hidden fees?

Really. Our scholarship guidance is completely free. For full-service packages, we publish every cost upfront. The only surprise we believe in is how smooth the process can actually be when done right.

Can parents be involved in the process?

Absolutely. We encourage it. We provide regular updates, clear timelines, and direct contact channels. Parents often have the best questions — and we have the answers. You're not handing your child to strangers; you're partnering with people who've walked the same path.
